**Recommendation: (A) server-side.** The plugin's Go server should run one receive-only WHEP client per live stream, with pion/webrtc v4. It keeps a rolling window on disk, cut into segments that each start on a keyframe. A clip is cut from that window with no re-encode and written as a normal MP4 (H264 + Opus, header at the front). Trimming is also lossless. I built and ran this against a real Broadcast Box v2.0.2 compiled from source on localhost. It works end to end: about 4% of one core per 6 Mbit/s stream, about 25 MB of memory for the whole process, and audio/video stay in sync. Option (B) costs viewers a lot, loses quality or disturbs the stream for everyone, and cannot be verified, so I reject it.

## 1. How VillaNET talks WHEP today
- **The exchange:** `exchangeWHEP` (`server/broadcastbox.go:157-211`) POSTs the offer to `BroadcastBoxURL+"/api/whep"` with `Authorization: Bearer <streamKey>` and no Basic Auth. It returns the answer plus a session id read from `Location` (`:213-241`, which only accepts hex/uuid ids). The recorder can call it as-is, with a background context instead of `r.Context()`.
- **Handles:** `streamKeyForHandle` only resolves streams that are live right now (`handles.go:70-85`).
- **Viewers' sessions:** `handleWHEP` (`api.go:608-680`) spends the peek before the exchange (`:645-648`). Afterwards it records either `rememberPeek` or `watchers().record` (`:661-665`).
- **Viewer count:** `poller.go:259` sets `counted := stills.counted(source.Sessions, now)`, and `Viewers: len(counted)` at `:268`. `stills.counted` (`stills.go:707-720`) only removes peeks.
- **"Who's watching":** `watchers.list` counts every session it does not know as a stranger (`watchers.go:186-197`, `strangers++` at `:193`).
- **Consequence:** the recorder's session id has to be removed inside or right after `counted`. Otherwise every recorded stream shows one extra viewer and "+1" on its card. I confirmed the recorder does appear in real BB's `/api/status` `sessions[]` under the same id as `Location`.

## 2. How Broadcast Box v2.0.2 treats a subscriber (source, tag v2.0.2)
- **No WHEP DELETE:** the handler accepts only POST and PATCH (`internal/server/handlers/whep.go:20-23`). It answers 201 with `Location: /api/whep/<uuid>` and two Link headers (`:77-82`). Closing our peer connection ends the BB session in the same second; I saw ICE "closed" followed immediately by `HandleWHEPClose`.
- **Answers are complete, not trickled.** BB waits for its own candidate gathering before answering (`internal/webrtc/whep.go:53,76`).
- **A POST for a key that isn't live** still creates a session (`GetOrAddSession`, `whep.go:22`). The recorder must only connect to live handles.
- **Codecs:** H264 (seven payload types), AV1, VP9 profiles 0 and 2, H265, and Opus. There is no VP8 (`internal/webrtc/codecs/codecs.go:32-145`).
  - BB rewrites the payload type on every packet to match the source codec (`track_multi_codec.go:128-151`). The recorder therefore registers the same codecs and payload types.
  - Real BB accepted all four video codecs in its answer to my offer.
- **Timestamps:** video timestamps restart at 5000 for each session (`sessions/whep/whep.go:25-26`, `packet_writer.go:70`). Audio is passed through with the publisher's original timestamps (`packet_writer.go:13-29`; `whip/writers.go:62` sets no time offset). The two tracks share no base, so the recorder lines them up by arrival time.
- **Keyframes:**
  - When ICE connects, BB sends a PLI (keyframe request) to the publisher (`sessions/whep/handlers.go:20-21`). It then drops video and keeps sending PLIs until a keyframe arrives (`packet_writer.go:45`).
  - That keyframe check only works for H264 (`whip/writers.go:217-229`). For AV1, VP9 and H265 every packet counts as a keyframe, so the recorder must detect keyframes itself.
  - Even for H264, pion's FU-A reassembly only returns the NAL unit on its last fragment (`pion/rtp codecs/h264_packet.go:288-310`). If the publisher sends no SPS/PPS packet before an IDR, BB can let a session start on a partial keyframe.
  - I saw this once: with ffmpeg's WHIP muxer as publisher, the recorder lost one GOP (~2 s) at start-up. With a pion publisher it lost nothing.
- **Subscriber PLIs reach the publisher with no rate limit** (`session/routines.go:34-35` to `whip/peerconnection.go:59-75`).
- **Simulcast:** each session gets whichever layer's packet arrives first (`writers.go:199-205`, `whep/whep.go:163-175`). `POST /api/layer/<id>` can change it (`handlers/layer_change.go`; note `:32` dereferences the session before checking it exists).
- **The publisher dropping does not end subscriber sessions.** The BB session stays open while any viewer session exists (`session/session.go:128-134, 166-179`). A returning OBS is attached to the existing sessions (`AddHost` `:53-89`, which calls `updateHostWHEPSessionsSnapshot`). So the recorder must close itself when the poller stops seeing the stream (after `OfflineGraceChecks`). Otherwise it keeps BB's session alive.
- **ICE:**
  - `NAT_1_TO_1_IP` is added on top of the normal addresses, not in place of them (`ICEAddressRewriteAppend`, `internal/webrtc/settings.go:187-216`).
  - The real answer listed every host address on the UDP mux port plus `203.0.113.10:23478 typ host`, so LAN addresses are always offered.
  - UDP mux setup is at `:87-92, 123-185`; `INTERFACE_FILTER` at `:94-105`.
  - TCP candidates appear only with `TCP_MUX_ADDRESS`/`TCP_MUX_FORCE` (`:41-85`). `NETWORK_TYPES` is effectively ignored because of an inverted error check (`:54-56`).
- **Reachability:** the origin firewall allows UDP 3478 from anywhere (`LOCKDOWN.md:33`). A Go client on 192.168.0.101 should therefore connect, as long as the Mattermost host's own firewall lets the replies back in.
- **BB ships the same idea as an example:** `examples/recording/main.go:38-125` is a pion receive-only WHEP recorder.

## 3. Option A as prototyped
Prototype directory: `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-user-Documents-Broadcast-Box-Plugin/f246a2f2-7be9-4da0-8cf3-a9bade7355be/scratchpad/clips/capture/proto/`. `recorder.go` and `ring.go` are the code the plugin would use; `fakebb.go` and `whippub.go` are test-only.

**Connection setup** (`recorder.go:34-84`):
- Its own MediaEngine with BB's payload types and codec parameters.
- `ConfigureNack` and `ConfigureRTCPReports` only.
- SettingEngine: UDP4 only, `ice.MulticastDNSModeDisabled`, and `SetRemoteIPFilter` set to BB's LAN IP.
- `Configuration{}` with no ICE servers, so nothing leaves the LAN.

**Receiving** (`:235-335`):
- `samplebuilder` with `codecs.H264Packet{IsAVC:true}` for video and `codecs.OpusPacket` for audio.
- Keyframe gating with mediacommon `h264`, collecting SPS/PPS, and a PLI on unrecoverable loss (at most once a second).
- Each track's timestamps are anchored to arrival time, and re-anchored on any jump over a second.

**Disk ring** (`ring.go`):
- Records are written to segment files that start on a keyframe.
- Memory holds only an index of about 80 entries per second, roughly 1 MB for 5 minutes.
- The oldest segment is evicted once the next one starts at or before now minus the window, and there is a hard byte cap (`:133-162`).
- `exportClip` (`:181-257`) builds an `mediacommon/v2 pkg/formats/pmp4` Presentation. Sample data is read from the segment files while the MP4 is written, so nothing is buffered in memory.
- `trimDraft` (`:292`) re-cuts a draft with `pmp4` Unmarshal then Marshal.

**Results:**

| Test | CPU | Memory | Clip | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Real BB v2.0.2, 6.09 Mbit/s, 40 s | 4.2% of one core | heap 6.3 MB, RSS 25.5 MB | 20 s draft written in 21 ms; trim in 15 ms | ICE paired only with the LAN host candidate on the mux port |
| Real BB, flash/beep sync source | 3.8% | – | – | audio minus video −7.5 ms, constant over 20 s, no drift |
| Fake BB loopback, 5.95 Mbit/s | 3.2% | RSS 25.6 MB | ring on disk 24 MB for a 30 s window | – |

- **Valid files:** every draft and trim decoded with `ffmpeg -xerror`. Video is H264 High 1280x720; audio is Opus 48 kHz stereo, aligned with an edit list.
- **Playback:** Chromium 152 (the engine the Mattermost desktop app uses) played the file with both tracks decoding and no dropped frames. Seeking worked only when the server supported Range requests, so serve clips with `http.ServeContent`.
- **Trimming:** a 5 s in-point snapped back to the 4 s keyframe (2 s GOP). The out-point is exact, because OBS's WHIP output has no B-frames.
- **Binary size:** the plugin binary for linux-amd64 grows from 21.6 to 26.7 MB (gzipped 8.09 to 9.90 MB). Everything is pure Go and builds with `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
- **Sync caveat:** an earlier 80 ms offset came from my test publisher's ticker skipping ticks; it was not the recorder.

**Bounded design:**
- **Ring size:** the window is the admin's maximum clip length plus one 6 s segment plus one GOP. Per-stream cap is window × 12 Mbit/s (about 460 MB at 5 minutes), plus a global disk budget, a free-space check, and a maximum number of recorders (for example 4).
- **Disk, not RAM:** a 375 MB ring in memory would be roughly 750 MB resident once Go's garbage collector headroom is counted.
- **Directory:** an absolute path setting, defaulting to `/var/tmp/...`. Do not use `os.TempDir()`: `/tmp` is tmpfs (RAM) on Debian 13 (`findmnt` on this machine). Do not use the plugin bundle directory either: it is deleted on upgrade (`mattermost server/channels/app/plugin_install.go:511,621`), and the plugin process runs with no working directory set (`server/public/plugin/supervisor.go:59`).
- **Cleanup:** wipe the ring directory on activate and deactivate. A restart loses the buffer.

**Always record, or only while watched?** I recommend recording every live stream that is not a 24/7 channel, for as long as it is live. The poller starts a recorder when it sees the stream and stops it after the offline grace period.
- The owner wrote "chat/viewers", and a streamer may want to clip their own stream while nobody is watching.
- The cost is small (about 4% of a core and about 0.75 MB/s of disk writes per stream), and the "last N minutes" are always there.
- The cheaper alternative is an admin switch that records only while someone is watching: start on a non-peek `handleWHEP`, and keep going while `Viewers > 0` plus a linger equal to the maximum clip length.
- 24/7 channels should be excluded, matching `previewable` (`stills.go`).

**Failure modes and their handling:**
- ICE blocked (Mattermost host firewall, `INTERFACE_FILTER`, or the BB URL pointing through the proxy): retry with backoff, disable the Clip button with a reason, and add settings for the media IP and the UDP port range.
- OBS reconnects or the resolution changes: start a new "epoch"; a clip never spans two.
- Codec change, or AV1/H265/VP9: extra depacketizers are needed. mediacommon can mux them, but HEVC will not play in Firefox.
- Simulcast: BB may hand the recorder a low layer; fix with `/api/layer`.
- Disk full: stop the recorder and log it.
- Recorder start-up: the PLI makes OBS send one extra keyframe to everyone, once per stream start. The recorder must never send PLIs on a timer.

## 4. Option B (MediaRecorder in each viewer's browser)
- **Chrome re-encodes when you give a type.** Default 2.5 Mbit/s (`chromium media_recorder.cc:61`). I measured 4 tiles at 720p30: the renderer went from 105% to 207% of a core, i.e. +102% (about 25% of a core per tile). Output was 2.85 Mbit/s VP8, a quality loss from the 6 Mbit/s source.
- **Chrome passthrough (no type given) has its own problems:**
  - It only applies when no type is given (`media_recorder_handler.cc:475, 636-645`).
  - H264 then comes out as `video/x-matroska;codecs=avc1` (`:822-830`), which Firefox and Safari won't play without a server-side remux.
  - It asks for a keyframe on start, and again whenever 100 frames pass without one (`video_track_recorder.cc:1069-1070, 1140-1141`; `key_frame_request_processor.cc:35-37`).
  - Measured: +7% CPU for 4 tiles, but 7 PLIs per tile in 20 s. In production BB forwards every one to OBS, so every viewer gets extra keyframes.
- **Firefox** records only VP8 in WebM, always re-encoding in software (`dom/media/MediaRecorder.cpp:346-395`).
- **Safari** re-encodes raw frames to H264/AAC in MP4 (`WebCore MediaRecorderPrivateEncoder.cpp:142-143, 452-466`).
- **No usable rolling buffer from `timeslice`.** Only the first chunk carries the WebM header (measured magic `1a45dfa3`; later chunks start mid-stream). Old chunks can't be dropped, so the recorder would have to be restarted per segment, which leaves gaps at the seams and, in passthrough, triggers another keyframe request each time.
- **Upload and trust:** the browser would have to upload 94–375 MB. The window only covers what that tab had open. The server cannot check the upload is the real stream, so anyone could game Clips and the Best Clipper trophy.

## 5. Libraries and APIs to use
- **WebRTC:** `github.com/pion/webrtc/v4` v4.2.22, plus `pion/interceptor` v0.1.49, `pion/rtp/codecs`, `pion/rtcp`, `pion/ice/v4`, and `webrtc/v4/pkg/media/samplebuilder`.
- **MP4 and H264 parsing:** `github.com/bluenviron/mediacommon/v2` v2.9.5 — `pkg/formats/pmp4` (writes the header first; `Sample.GetPayload` reads lazily; `Track.TimeOffset` becomes an edit list, `pmp4/track.go:322-355`), `pkg/formats/mp4/codecs` `H264`/`Opus`, and `pkg/codecs/h264`.
- **Not used:** ffmpeg, `os/exec`, cgo, STUN.

## 6. Where it plugs into VillaNET
- **New store:** `server/clips_recorder.go` with `p.recorders()` behind a `sync.Once`, following the pattern of `plugin.go:359-364`.
- **Start/stop:** driven from the poller after `decorate`; stop everything in `OnDeactivate` (`plugin.go:489`) and when the feature is switched off.
- **Exchange:** `p.exchangeWHEP(ctx, cfg, key, offer)`.
- **Hiding:** filter recorder session ids at `poller.go:259`, or inside `stills.counted`.
- **Clip flow:**
  - Clicking Clip exports a draft MP4, served by `ServeContent` for preview. The response includes the keyframe times so the trim handles can snap to them.
  - Publishing runs `trimDraft`.
  - Durable storage and retention are a separate question.
- **Docs:** `LOCKDOWN.md` ("What the plugin touches") gains media to UDP 3478, and `/api/layer` if used.

I recommend storing clips as plain files under `<FileSettings.Directory>/villanet/clips/` and serving them through VillaNET's own authenticated route with `http.ServeContent`. If the server is not on the local storage driver, the feature switches itself off and tells admins why. Sources:
- **Mattermost:** fetched from `master` on 2026-10-01; tags are named where older releases differ.
- **Plugin API:** the module the plugin builds against, `server/public@v0.4.4` in `~/go/pkg/mod`.
- **VillaNET:** paths are relative to `/home/user/Documents/Broadcast Box Plugin`.
- **Note:** `server/plugin.go:21` and `plugin.json` both say version 2.8.0, not 2.9.0.

## 1. Storage of clip files

**(a) Mattermost files (`UploadFile` / `GetFile` / `ReadFile`, or upload sessions): reject.**
- **Whole files in memory:**
  - `UploadFile(data []byte, …)` (plugin `api.go:888`) builds the whole file in memory. It then passes the bytes to every plugin's `FileWillBeUploaded` hook (`app/file.go:1106-1124`).
  - `GetFile` and `ReadFile` (`plugin_api.go:1105-1111`, `app/file.go:1381-1393`) return a `[]byte`, so the whole clip crosses the plugin RPC.
  - pluginapi's `FileService.Upload` and `Get` (`pluginapi/file.go:19-25, 69-77`) are just `io.ReadAll` wrappers around these.
- **Streaming upload exists:** `CreateUploadSession` and `UploadData` (`api.go:1245-1257`). `UploadData` streams over the plugin connection (`client_rpc.go:1316-1336`). The Calls plugin uploads recordings this way (`mattermost-plugin-calls server/bot_api.go:125-128, 155-170`).
- **It needs a channel:** the channel must exist and not be deleted (`app/upload.go:144-153`), and the first part must be at least 5 MB (`upload.go:23, 247-264`).
- **Who can read `/api/v4/files/{id}`:** the handler loads the file's channel (`api4/file.go:544-548`). After that, only the uploader or someone with read permission on that channel can fetch it (`:594-605`). Team members can read public channels (`app/authorization.go:466-476`).
  - Files sent with `UploadFile` never get a channel id (`file.go:1066-1160`), so they can't be served until attached to a post.
  - Range requests do work there: the handler ends in `http.ServeContent` (`platform/shared/web/files.go:42-55`).
- **`FileSettings.MaxFileSize`** (default 100 MB, `model/config.go:1887-1888`) is only enforced on the public REST path (`api4/upload.go:81`). Plugin uploads skip it.
- **The deciding problem: no deletion.**
  - The plugin API has no way to delete a file (checked every Delete/Remove/File method in `api.go`).
  - `DeletePost` only marks the file record deleted (`app/post.go:2315-2319`, `sqlstore/file_info_store.go:457-468`); the bytes stay on disk.
  - No open-source job removes unattached files (`server/channels/jobs` listing).
  - So a 30-day expiry could never free any disk space.

**(b) Plugin-managed directory inside the server's data directory: recommend.**
- **Locating it:**
  - Read `FileSettings.DriverName` and `Directory` from `GetUnsanitizedConfig` (`plugin_api.go:111-113`, a plain config clone). `GetConfig` also works, because these two fields aren't redacted (`config.go:5341-5358`).
  - Only proceed when the driver is `model.ImageDriverLocal`.
  - The plugin process is started with no working directory of its own (`plugin/supervisor.go:59`), so it shares the server's. The default `./data/` therefore resolves to the same place for both.
- **Layout:** files under `villanet/clips/<id>.webm|mp4` and `<id>.jpg`, drafts under `villanet/clips/drafts/`.
  - Stay out of the server's `plugins/` folder, where plugin bundles live (`app/plugin_install.go:92-93, 647-649`, `app/plugin.go:889-901`).
  - Copy Mattermost's own permissions: directories 0750, files 0600 (`filestore/localstore.go:140, 160`).
  - Publish atomically: write a temp file, then `os.Rename`.
  - Never store anything in the plugin bundle directory, which is replaced on upgrade.
- **Serving:** open the file and call `http.ServeContent`. That gives Range, `If-Range` and HEAD, with low memory use (checked with a throwaway Go program: 206 response with `Content-Range`).
  - Set the `Content-Type` from a stored allowlist. Go recognises both `video/webm` and `video/mp4` from the first bytes (tested), so check those on upload.
  - Add `nosniff` and the sandbox CSP that `writeImage` uses (`server/brand.go:135-167`).
- **Auth:**
  - A `<video src>` GET carries the session cookie.
  - GET requests skip the CSRF check (`app/plugin_requests.go:293-297`).
  - Mattermost removes any client-sent user header and sets `Mattermost-User-Id` itself (`:193-194, 282-284`), which `server/api.go:110-116` already relies on.
  - Range headers reach the plugin (`client_rpc.go:493-503`), and gzip only wraps `/static/plugins` (`web/static.go:42-45`).
- **Costs:**
  - Every `Write` becomes two RPC calls (`plugin/http.go:88-96`), so buffer the response at 512 KB to 1 MB.
  - The server's `ReadTimeout` and `WriteTimeout` are 300 s (`app/server.go:1136-1138`, defaults at `config.go:132-133`).
    - Responses: no single response can last longer than that. A `<video>` simply re-requests by Range.
    - Uploads: browser uploads must be chunked (about 8 MB each).
- **Uploads must send `X-CSRF-Token`.** Without it, Mattermost reads the request body itself:
  - On `master` it is capped at `MaximumPayloadSizeBytes` (default 300000), so a clip gets a 413 (`plugin_requests.go:271-281, 299-313`).
  - On v9.11 and v10.11 it reads the whole body into server memory (`v10.11.0:179-186`, `v9.11.0:158-166`).
  - `client.ts:7-21` only sends the token when the `MMCSRF` cookie exists, so the clip uploader should refuse to upload without it.
- **S3:** not supported. This fails closed, with the reason shown to admins on `/me` and in the clip admin screen. Clips already on disk and all KV data are left alone.
- **HA:** works only if the data directory is shared between nodes. In-memory caches are per node, like stills.

**(c) Importing a filestore package: not now.**
- `server/public` has no filestore (its packages are `model`, `plugin`, `pluginapi`, `shared/*`, `utils`).
- The real one is `server/platform/shared/filestore` (interface at `filesstore.go:26-45`). It lives in module `github.com/mattermost/mattermost/server/v8` (`server/go.mod:1`), which pulls in the whole server's dependencies plus S3/Azure SDKs and can drift from the running server version.
- It would also need the S3 secret key, and talking to S3 conflicts with "no external calls" unless the bucket is on the LAN. Keep it as the documented path if the server ever moves to S3.

## 2. Metadata (KV)

Follow the schedule's pattern: a few fixed-name documents, each carrying its own `v`, every write through `casUpdate` (`server/community.go:16-35, 215-250`). Never use `KVList` for anything that must stay accurate; it can silently miss keys (`server/links.go:170-181`). Key names are limited to 150 characters (`model/plugin_key_value.go:13`).

- **`clips`** — `{v, clips:[…]}`, capped at about 500 entries. Each entry holds:
  - id (`newID`, `community.go:177`), stream `handle` (never the key), `streamerId`, `streamerLink` (manual or username, from `resolveUser`, `poller.go:389-405`), `streamTitle`
  - `clipperId`, `title` (passed through `cleanText` and `withoutOwnKey`, `community.go:191-209`), `createdAt`, `startAt`, `durationMs`
  - optional trim in/out points, `bytes`, `mime`, `codecs`, `width`, `height`, `thumb` version, a server-only file name
  - `voters: {userId: votedAtMs}`, and optional `settling` and `voided` flags
  - `expiresAt` is calculated as `createdAt` plus the current retention setting rather than stored, so changing the setting applies to existing clips. The API returns it.
- **Votes** go inside the clip entry: one atomic write per vote, and the count is the number of voters.
  - The request says the desired state (`{up: true|false}`), never "toggle", so retries and double-clicks are harmless (rule 1 at `community.go:28-35`).
  - Refuse: votes on your own clip, votes from bots, and votes on settling or expired clips.
- **`clips_tally`** — the all-time numbers that survive expiry:
  - `clippers: {userId: {up, clips, lastUpAt}}`, built from clips that have been settled.
  - `settled: {clipId: at}`, pruned once a clip is gone from `clips`.
  - `holder: {userId, since, up}`.

# VillaNET Clips: UX design report

The design follows patterns the panel already uses:

- **Clip button:** a scissors button (✂) on the picture, in the controls bar that appears when you point at a playing tile.
- **Editor:** a wide dialog laid over the whole window, built like the Top Streamers card, with a trimmer that has two handles.
- **Clips section:** a dialog opened from a new clapperboard button in the header, next to the trophy. A compact "Clips" row of cards at the bottom of the panel also opens it.
- **Best Clipper:** a gold clapperboard badge, drawn the same way as the crown and calendar badges. It shows beside names in posts, in the profile popover and in the trophy dialog.

Everything below is checked against the code. File references are relative to the repo unless they say otherwise.

---

## 0. Facts in the code the design depends on

- **Controls live on the picture and appear only while someone is pointing at it.** The power switch sits in the middle; sound, pop-out and full screen run along the bottom (`Player.tsx:336-374`, `Hud.tsx:9-38`).
  - The bottom buttons are plain 30px icons, not pills. Code comment: "over a picture, a row of outlined lozenges is a row of labels" (`Hud.tsx:430-444`, styles `.vntv-hud-button` at `styles.ts:1284`).
  - Disabled-looking buttons are avoided. The idle set has "no controls at all … not even greyed out" (README 1284).
- **Sound is a radio button, not a per-tile mute.** "Nothing is ever unmuted except by a click" (README 1446-1449).
  - The sound has to be taken inside the click itself (`Player.tsx:235-254`). A layout effect moves it between tiles synchronously (`Player.tsx:184-197`).
- **Full screen is the player frame itself** (`frame.requestFullscreen()` at `Player.tsx:283-299`). Full screen uses the browser's top layer, so a portal on `document.body` (where the dialogs render) is not visible while a tile is full screen.
- **The dialog pattern is the Top Streamers card** (`LeaderboardModal.tsx`):
  - It is a portal on `document.body` (`:239-243`, `:273`), styled `.vntv-modal` with z-index 1060, above Mattermost's own modal layer at 1050 (`styles.ts:3194`).
  - The card is the dark `#080103` with a `--vntv-outline` border and 12px corners (`styles.ts:3207-3218`).
  - The header has an icon, a title in the Oswald display font in capitals, and a × (`styles.ts:3220-3265`).
  - Escape is handled with a capture-phase keydown listener that stops propagation (`LeaderboardModal.tsx:247-264`).
  - It has **no focus trap**. The editor should add one.
- **Destructive admin actions need a second, separate click:** `CONFIRM_MS` 4000 and `CONFIRM_MIN_MS` 500, with the label changing to "Click again to block …" (`AdminStills.tsx:22-27, 196-213`).
- **"Disabled but still explains itself"** uses `aria-disabled`, not `disabled` (`UpNext.tsx:523`, `MediaProfile.tsx:267`). Shortcuts are advertised with `aria-keyshortcuts` (`UpNext.tsx:545`).
- **A card with a second action is two sibling buttons.** "A button cannot hold another button" (`LiveCard.tsx:65-69`). Upvoting on a clip card works the same way.
- **The snapshot must be identical for every viewer:** "Nothing here may be specific to a viewer" (`server/plugin.go:221-224`).
  - Clip-wide facts (clips on or off, clip length, Best Clipper, how much of each stream is recorded) can go on the snapshot.
  - Anything per person ("did I upvote this", "my drafts", "can I delete this") needs its own endpoint.
- **The server never decodes video.** Live Now stills are 480×270 JPEGs made by a browser on a canvas (`webapp/src/stills.ts:32-33, 430`; `server/stills.go:118-121`). Clip thumbnails should be made the same way: by the editor's browser, at publish time.
- **24/7 channels are excluded from stills and airtime** ("it is a channel, not a person", README 758). They should be excluded from clipping too.
- **Panel height is precious.** The airtime boards were moved out of the panel because they took 55% of the scroll, and "Out of the panel entirely is better than collapsed inside it" (README 1013-1020). Anything new below the set must also glide with it (`Sidebar.tsx:423-435`).
- **Mattermost hooks needed, checked in source:**
  - `registerRootComponent` and `registerNeedsTeamRoute` both exist at v9.0.0 (`webapp/channels/src/plugins/registry.ts:94` and `:918`). Plugin team routes render at `/:team/<pluginId>/<route>` (`team_controller.tsx` v9.0.0 `:227-233`).
  - Mattermost's own pop-out windows also render `<Pluggable pluggableName='Root'/>` (master `components/popout_controller/popout_controller.tsx:53`).
  - A same-site link pasted in chat is navigated in-app unless its path starts with `plugins`, `files` or `help` (v9.0.0 `utils/url.tsx:175-200`; master `utils/markdown/renderer.tsx:169-177` sets `data-link`; `utils/utils.tsx:1364` calls `getHistory().push`).
- **Where the media comes from changes the UX.** This design assumes the plugin server keeps a rolling recording of each live stream.
  - Broadcast Box ships a Go WHEP recording client at the v2.0.2 tag (`examples/recording/main.go`; curl returned 200 at `v2.0.2`). It uses pion's `h264writer` and `oggwriter`.
  - Server-side recording means **anyone can clip the full last 2:00, even if they tuned in 10 seconds ago**.
  - If it ends up browser-side (MediaRecorder on the tile), the "only N seconds so far" state becomes the normal case: you can only clip what you have watched. Every tile also pays for an encoder. The UX strongly prefers server-side; the backend research covers whether it's feasible.

## 1. The Clip button

### Where it lives

It goes in the HUD bar of every playing tile, in the right-hand group, left of the pop-out link and full screen:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                             │
│                    (⏻)                      │   power switch, middle (unchanged)
│                                             │
│ 🔊 ━━━━━○─────            ✂   ⧉   ⛶        │   .vntv-hud-bar
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  (face) Dave   Arma 3 ops night ▸ ticker…        TileInfo (unchanged)
```

- **Component:** a `HudButton` with a new `ScissorsIcon` (line style, `currentColor`, 16px, like the other HUD icons; `icons.tsx:10-20`). It goes in `Player.tsx` between `.vntv-hud-spacer` and the pop-out link (`Player.tsx:359-369`).
- **Why that spot:** the left group is about sound. The right group is "do something with this picture", and full screen stays in the corner where people expect it.
- **In a 2×2 grid,** tiles are at least about 300px wide (one column below a 620px container; `styles.ts:641-656`). Five icons plus a shrinking volume slider fit; the slider gives way first (`flex: 0 1 120px; min-width: 0` at `styles.ts:1330-1343`).
- **Not on:**
  - `WaitingTile`, whose stream has dropped. It has no bar (`Player.tsx:415-435`).
  - The No Signal set, which has no HUD at all.
  - Live Now cards: you clip what you are watching.
  - 24/7 channels (see §0).

### Keyboard

- Pressing **C** while focus is anywhere in the tile clips. Attach `onKeyDown` to `.vntv-player`; a focused HUD control or the title ticker bubbles up to it.
- Ignore the key when any modifier is held, because **Ctrl/⌘+C must stay copy**, and when an input method is composing (`keys.ts:8-10`).
- Advertise it with `aria-keyshortcuts='c'` and in the tooltip: "Clip the last 2:00 (C)".
- **No global shortcut.** A plain letter key would land in the message box when focus isn't in the tile.

### States

How much of each stream has been recorded comes from the snapshot: `stream.clipFrom`, the instant the recording of this session began (absent means the stream can't be clipped). The tile works out the seconds itself each second, so the label never lags a 15-second poll.

| State | Button | Accessible name / tooltip |
|---|---|---|
| Clips switched off, 24/7 channel | **not rendered** | — |
| Ready (recorded ≥ admin length) | normal | "Clip the last 2 minutes" / title "Clip the last 2:00 (C)" |
| Partial (5 s ≤ recorded < length) | normal, plus a tiny "0:47" corner tag on the icon | "Clip the last 47 seconds — all that has been recorded so far" |
| Warming up (< 5 s recorded, recording just started) | `aria-disabled`, 40% opacity | "Clipping starts in a few seconds" |
| Paused publisher | `aria-disabled` | "Paused — nothing to clip right now" |
| Recording broken (server lost its session) | `aria-disabled` | "Clipping isn't working on this stream just now" |
| Working (capture request in flight) | `aria-disabled`, icon pulses | "Clipping…" |

Use `aria-disabled` rather than `disabled` so the explanation tooltip still works.

### What a click does

1. **Same click:** if the tile is in full screen, call `document.exitFullscreen()`. Otherwise the editor's portal can't be seen.
2. The editor opens **immediately**, in its "cutting" state. Opening it at once is the click's feedback, so the HUD needs no lasting "clipped!" state. The HUD goes back to sleep after its normal 2.6 seconds (`Hud.tsx:41`).
3. The request sends `{handle}`, the opaque per-stream handle (`types.ts:2-4`), never a stream key. The server freezes the last *N* seconds into a **draft** and returns its id, length, start instant, keyframe times and a video URL.
4. The live tile keeps playing underneath with its sound. The sound only steps aside when the preview is played (§2).

- **The editor isn't lost if someone closes the panel mid-edit.** Mattermost unmounts the sidebar on close (README: "Mattermost unmounts the panel when it is closed").
- **One host serves every entry point.** The header button (a separate React tree; `identity.ts:7-11`), the in-panel row and a link route all open the same host.

### The trimmer (`ClipTrimmer.tsx`)

**It has three focusable `role="slider"` thumbs: Start, Playhead and End** (the WAI-ARIA multi-thumb slider pattern).

- `aria-label="Start of the clip"`, `aria-valuetext="0:38 of 2:00, on a keyframe"`.
- Snaps to keyframe ticks while dragging.
- Arrow keys move to the previous or next keyframe; Shift+Arrow and Page Up/Down move ±10 s; Home goes to 0.

**End:**
- `aria-label="End of the clip"`, `aria-valuetext="1:23 — the clip is 45 seconds"`.
- Arrow keys ±1 s; Shift and Page Up/Down ±10 s; End goes to the end of the draft.

**Limits:**
- Each thumb's `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` reflects the other thumb.
- **Minimum length is 5 s**; the handles cannot cross.
- **The trimmer only shrinks the clip.** The draft is the admin's length, and "clip it down further" never means longer.

**Playhead:**
- `aria-label="Position"`. It can scrub the **whole** draft, including the dimmed parts, so you can find where the moment starts.
- **Dragging a handle pauses and scrubs to the handle's frame**, so you see exactly where the cut lands. On release the preview stays paused there.

**Dialog shortcuts** (ignored while focus is in the title field):
- **Space:** play/pause.
- **I / O:** set start/end at the playhead.
- The ✂ tooltip lists them: "I and O set the start and end at the playhead."

**Snapping (why the start moves in steps):**
- The server cuts without decoding, so a clip can only begin on a keyframe. Without B-frames the end can be frame-exact.
- The draft response carries the keyframe times. Draw them as faint `┊` ticks above the track.
- Hint, worked out from the median gap between keyframes:
  - Normally: "The start moves in steps: a clip has to begin on a keyframe — a full picture the stream sends every 2 seconds or so."
  - If the gap is more than 5 s: "This stream only sends a full picture every 8 seconds, so the start moves in 8-second steps. A keyframe interval of 2 in the streamer's encoder settings fixes it."
- For context, Broadcast Box's own ffmpeg example uses `-r 25 -g 50`, a 2-second GOP (BB v2.0.2 README:68).
- If the backend writes an MP4 edit list instead, snapping can be dropped and the ticks become information only.

**Pointer and touch:**
- Use the ImageCropper drag pattern: `setPointerCapture` on the handle (`ImageCropper.tsx:237-264`).
- Handles are drawn about 12px wide with a 44×44 transparent hit area.
- The track has `touch-action: none` so dragging doesn't scroll the dialog.
- Tapping the bare track seeks the playhead; it never moves a handle.
- Optional: drag the selected band to slide the whole window, keeping its length.

**Optional filmstrip:** after load, seek about 12 points and draw small frames into the track background. Do it progressively and skip it when reduced motion or Save-Data is set.

### Title field

- **Do not prefill it with the stream title.** Every clip from the same evening would then be called "Arma 3 ops night", and the shelf becomes unreadable. The stream title is already shown on the context line.
- Placeholder: **"What happened?"**. `maxLength` 80; a counter appears from 60 characters.
- If left empty, it publishes as "Dave, 3 Oct 21:04", the streamer plus local time.
- **Initial focus goes to this field**, so typing names the clip at once. **Enter publishes**, consistent with the stream-title box, where Enter commits (`Sidebar.tsx:1011-1015`).

### Thumbnail

- At Publish, the editor draws the frame at **in-point + 0.5 s** to a 480×270 JPEG and uploads it with the publish request. That is the same size and validation as stills.

- **Native `controls` are fine here.** The rule against them is about *live* video (README "The player": a paused live picture is a frozen frame of something that has moved on); a recorded clip is exactly where pause and seek make sense. They are also accessible for free.
  - `preload="metadata"`.
  - Video is served by the plugin with Range support so seeking works. GET with cookie auth already works for `<img src>` stills; the same should hold for `<video>`.
- **Same sound rule:** playing a clip with sound releases the live tile's sound, and closing gives it back.
- **Upvote:**

- **Delete:**
  - Shown to the clipper, **the streamer who was clipped**, and system admins.
  - Two clicks: "Delete" → "Click again — its 14 upvotes stop counting".

- **Gone** (expired or deleted while open): "This clip has gone — it expired or somebody deleted it."

## 4. The Best Clipper trophy

### Rules (owner-facing copy)

- One holder, all time, by **total upvotes received on their clips**. No runner-up is ever shown.
- **Ties keep the holder.** You have to beat the holder to take the title. The rule is stable and easy to explain.
- **Expired clips keep counting** ("all time"). **Deleted clips stop counting**, otherwise moderation couldn't take an award back. The delete confirmation says so.
- No votes on your own clips; one vote per person per clip.
- Nobody holds it until somebody has 1 upvote.
- On the snapshot (the same for everyone): `bestClipper: {userId, username, displayName, votes, clips, bestClipId?, bestClipTitle?, bestClipVotes?}`.
